quote: Theorem 1. Let T ⇝ GMOTL − G(δ, ρ1, ω) and Y ⇝ GMOTL − G(δ, ρ2, ω). If ρ1 < ρ2, then T ≤lr Y. As a consequence, it follows that (T ≤hr Y, T ≤rhr Y, T ≤st Y).
family: generalized Marshall–Olkin Topp–Leone-G (GMOTL-G) family; combines GMO survival S_GMO(t; ρ, δ) = [ρ S(t)/(1 − ρ̄ S(t))]^δ (ρ > 0, ρ̄ = 1 − ρ, δ > 0) with Topp–Leone-G generator G_TLG(t; ω) = 1 − Ḡ(t)^{2ω}, ω > 0; parameters (δ, ρ, ω) plus baseline G
compared: GMO tilting parameter ρ1 vs ρ2; common δ, ω and baseline G

hypotheses.text: Let T ⇝ GMOTL − G(δ, ρ1, ω) and Y ⇝ GMOTL − G(δ, ρ2, ω)
hypotheses.formal: T ~ GMOTL-G(δ, ρ1, ω), Y ~ GMOTL-G(δ, ρ2, ω)

hypotheses.text: T is said to be smaller than Y in the likelihood ratio order (denoted by T ≤lr Y) if the ratio f(t)/g(t) is decreasing in t, for all t ≥ 0

conclusion.direction: T <=lr Y for ρ1 < ρ2 (hence T <=hr Y, T <=rhr Y, T <=st Y as printed)

ambiguity: The listed consequences include T ≤rhr Y; lr ⇒ rhr is a standard implication, consistent with the claim as printed. The proof's displayed derivative d/dt(f/g) is heavily garbled in the text layer but concludes negative when ρ1 < ρ2.
